question: Pravda alebo nepravda: chlieb v chladničke stvrdne rýchlejšie, ako keď leží na kuchynskej linke.
source_excerpt: the rate at which the starch crystals re-form is increased as heat is withdrawn

extra.why_interesting: Most people put bread in the fridge to keep it fresh, assuming cold preserves everything. In fact the cold speeds up staling, which overturns a common household habit.
extra.verification_notes: Fridge temperatures accelerate starch retrogradation, so bread stales/hardens faster than on the counter (https://iufost.org/iufostold/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/66-The-Complexities-of-Bread-Staling.pdf).

explanation: Chlieb netvrdne hlavne preto, že vysychá. Škrob v ňom znova kryštalizuje a najrýchlejšie sa to deje práve pri teplote chladničky. Preto pomôže, keď starší rožok na pár minút vložíte do horúcej rúry: kryštáliky sa roztopia a pečivo opäť zmäkne.

question: Slovo „chlieb“ si starí Slovania kedysi požičali od germánskych susedov. Ktoré anglické slovo pre bochník je jeho blízky príbuzný?

extra.why_interesting: Players assume 'chlieb' is as native as a word can get, the most basic Slavic word for the most basic food. It turns out to be a Germanic loanword. Saying 'chlieb' and 'hlaib' side by side lets anyone with a little English reason their way to 'loaf'. The payoff that 'lord' once meant 'guardian of the bread' adds a second surprise.
extra.verification_notes: Proto-Slavic *xlěbъ is a Germanic loan from *hlaibaz, which is also the source of English 'loaf' (https://en.wiktionary.com/wiki/chleb).

explanation: Starogermánske „hlaib“ dalo nám chlieb a Angličanom loaf. Z toho istého slova vznikol aj anglický „lord“, pôvodne „hlāford“, teda doslova strážca chleba.
